title: Collatz Steps
problem: Read one positive integer N. Repeat these rules until the number becomes 1: if it is even, halve it; if it is odd, multiply it by 3 and add 1. Print how many steps it took. For example, 6 goes 6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, which is 8 steps, and 1 needs 0 steps.
starter_code:
# Read one positive integer N.
# Apply the even/odd rules until the number is 1, and print the number of steps.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Each step depends on whether the current number is even or odd, and you do not know in advance how many steps there will be.
hints.2: Use a loop that keeps going while the number is not 1. Inside it, use % to test for even or odd, change the number, and add one to a step counter. Use whole-number division (//) so the number stays an integer.

failure_explanation: Keep applying the rule until the number reaches 1, and count every change, including the last one that lands on 1. Start the counter at 0, because a starting number of 1 needs no steps. Use // and not / when halving so the number stays a whole number, and remember that an odd number becomes 3 times itself plus 1, not just 3 times itself.
